svg.title: What USPS pages say about a refund and how it differs from a claim, with no amounts or fees. Refund: money back for postage or fees when a service's own refund conditions are met, such as USPS at fault, too much charged, a paid service not provided, or a Priority Mail Express guarantee missed (DMM 604.9.2, 604.9.5). Claim: for insured mail that was lost, damaged or missing contents, a separate process on the USPS.com File a Claim page and in DMM 609. When to apply, counted from the mailing date: Priority Mail Express day 2 to 30, or day 30 to 60 with an extra service; extra services day 30 to 60; postage on other mail day 10 to 60 (DMM chart only). A window does not guarantee a refund; service conditions and exceptions apply (USPS.com refund page, DMM 604.9). Click-N-Ship label, counted from the print date: online in your account for a label printed within 30 days; for a label printed more than 30 but less than 60 days ago, email the Click-N-Ship Help Desk. The page also says up to 60 days and does not say what applies on day 60; timing alone does not guarantee a refund. Not refundable (DMM 604.9.2.4): COD, Priority Mail Express insurance, insured mail and Registered Mail fees after USPS accepts the item; unused stamps are exchanged. Priority Mail Express has its own exceptions (DMM 604.9.5.5).
